## `scripts/fp/asset_paths.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

First-person asset paths. Slice H owns this list and produces the files; every consumer loads them with load_scene() and falls back to the legacy asset or a procedural stand-in on null.

### Constants

- `PEOPLE_LEGACY_DIR = "res://models/real/people/"`
- `PEOPLE_RIGGED_DIR = "res://models/real/people_rigged/"`
- `VEHICLES_LEGACY_DIR = "res://models/real/vehicles/"`
- `VEHICLES_V2_DIR = "res://models/real/vehicles_v2/"`
- `STREET_DIR = "res://models/real/street/"`
- `TRAFFIC_LIGHT = STREET_DIR + "traffic_light.glb"`
- `PED_SIGNAL = STREET_DIR + "ped_signal.glb"`
- `STREET_SIGN = STREET_DIR + "street_sign.glb"`
- `STOP_SIGN = STREET_DIR + "stop_sign.glb"`
- `YIELD_SIGN = STREET_DIR + "yield_sign.glb"`
- `BUS_SHELTER = STREET_DIR + "bus_shelter.glb"`
- `BILLBOARD_POSTER = STREET_DIR + "billboard.glb"`
- `POSTER_FRAME = STREET_DIR + "poster_frame.glb"`
- `HOARDING = STREET_DIR + "hoarding.glb"`
- `CROSSWALK_RAMP = STREET_DIR + "curb_ramp.glb"`
- `BIKE_RACK = STREET_DIR + "bike_rack.glb"`
- `PARKING_METER = STREET_DIR + "parking_meter.glb"`
- `LEASE_SIGN = STREET_DIR + "lease_sign.glb"`
- `BOLLARD = "res://models/real/props/bollard.glb"`
- `BICYCLE = VEHICLES_V2_DIR + "bicycle.glb"`
- `PERSON_ANIMS = ["idle", "walk", "run", "talk", "sit"]`: Animation names every rigged person provides, as Godot lists them after import. H names the Blender actions "<name>-loop" (and "sit") so the importer sets LOOP_LINEAR; H's test confirms the suffix is stripped on 4.7.2. If it is not, H changes this list to the suffixed names.
- `PERSON_LOOPING = ["idle", "walk", "run", "talk"]`
- `WHEEL_NODES = ["Wheel_FL", "Wheel_FR", "Wheel_RL", "Wheel_RR"]`: Separate wheel nodes on vehicles_v2 road vehicles (origin at the hub, spin about local X).
- `BIKE_WHEEL_NODES = ["Wheel_F", "Wheel_R"]`
- `DRIVER_MARKERS = ["Pedal_L", "Pedal_R", "Wheel_L", "Wheel_R", "Cab_Roof"]`: Driver contact markers in vehicles_v2 road vehicles with a driver's seat (empties, like Seat_Driver): Pedal_L / Pedal_R at the ankle targets on the footwell floor (the driver's side is +X), Wheel_L / Wheel_R on the steering rim, Cab_Roof on the headliner above the seat. The drive feature seats the hero's feet and hands on them and sinks the hips until the head clears Cab_Roof, so the seated pose fits every cabin.
- `CRANK_NODE = "Crank"`: The bicycle's cranks and pedals (origin at the bottom bracket, spin about local X; the left pedal, on +X, straight up at rest).
- `BIKE_MARKERS = ["Pedal_L", "Pedal_R", "Handle_L", "Handle_R"]`: The bicycle's rider contact markers: Pedal_L / Pedal_R sit on the pedals and turn with the Crank, Handle_L / Handle_R on the grips. The rider's feet follow the pedals (drive/seat_pose.gd).
- `VEHICLE_LOD_SUFFIX = "_lod1.glb"`: Far LOD next to each vehicles_v2 model (<name>_lod1.glb): one mesh, wheels merged, at most 1,500 triangles, a few flat untextured materials (colour in the albedo); the lamp lenses are the emissive Light_Head / Light_Tail.
- `SIGNAL_NODE_PREFIXES = ["Signal_Red_", "Signal_Amber_", "Signal_Green_"]`: Traffic-signal lens nodes in TRAFFIC_LIGHT (<prefix><n>, one material each), and the pedestrian head nodes in TRAFFIC_LIGHT and PED_SIGNAL.
- `WALK_NODE_PREFIX = "Walk_"`
- `DONT_WALK_NODE_PREFIX = "DontWalk_"`
- `SIGN_TEXT_NODES = ["SignText_A", "SignText_B"]`: Name-blade anchors in TRAFFIC_LIGHT and STREET_SIGN: A runs along X facing +Z, B along Z facing +X.
- `POSTER_NODE_PREFIX = "Poster_"`: Node-name contracts inside H's GLBs (all optional; consumers fall back when absent). Poster_<n>: MeshInstance3D, one surface, material "Poster", UV 0..1, normal +Z in node space.
- `POSTER_SPOT_PREFIX = "PosterSpot_"`: PosterSpot_<n>: empty on a blank wall, +Z out of the wall, scale = poster size in units.
- `DOOR_SPOT_PREFIX = "Door_"`: Door_<n>: empty at the bottom centre of a doorway, +Z out, scale.y = leaf height.
- `COLBOX_PREFIX = "ColBox_"`: ColBox_<n>: empty, position = box centre, scale = half extents (collision proxy, no mesh).
- `CHARACTERS_DIR = "res://models/characters/"`: Realistic characters (slice HC, docs/fp/slices/HC-characters.md). Bodies are Microsoft Rocketbox avatars on Godot's humanoid skeleton (`%GeneralSkeleton`, metric, feet at y = 0, facing +Z). Scale each one under a `CharacterRoot` node: `scale = WS.M * h_target_m / rest_height_m`, with rest_height_m (stature to the skull top; hair and hats add up to 4 %) from CHAR_ROSTER. Animate with the gender's library added as the default library "" (clip names stay bare: "walk") and `root_motion_track = CHAR_ROOT_MOTION_TRACK`; loops then play in place. Every clip carries the metas `speed_mps` (Root speed on a skeleton whose hips are `speed_ref_hip_m` high: a body with hip_m from the roster covers speed_mps * hip_m / speed_ref_hip_m metres per second before CharacterRoot scaling) and `loop`; turns also carry `root_turn_deg`.
- `CHAR_BODIES_DIR = CHARACTERS_DIR + "bodies/"`
- `CHAR_ROSTER = CHARACTERS_DIR + "roster.json"`: roster.json: bodies (rest_height_m, hip_m, group, gender, lod1), job_pools, casual_pools, name_gender, height targets. Far LODs are CHAR_BODIES_DIR + "<Name>_lod1.glb".
- `CHAR_LIB_M = CHARACTERS_DIR + "anim/lib_m.tres"`
- `CHAR_LIB_F = CHARACTERS_DIR + "anim/lib_f.tres"`
- `HERO_M = CHAR_BODIES_DIR + "Male_Adult_06.glb"`
- `HERO_F = CHAR_BODIES_DIR + "Female_Adult_04.glb"`
- `CHAR_ROOT_MOTION_TRACK = "%GeneralSkeleton:Root"`
- `CHAR_LOOK_AXIS = SkeletonModifier3D.BONE_AXIS_PLUS_Z`: LookAtModifier3D.forward_axis for the Head and Neck bones of every character rig.
- `PERSON_TPS_ANIMS = [ "idle", "walk", "walk_fast", "run", "run_fast", "crouch_idle", "crouch_walk", "jump_s...`: Clips the player uses (both libraries hold them, plus AP.PERSON_ANIMS and the crowd extras).
- `DOG_SHIBA = "res://models/real/animals/shiba_inu.glb"`: Quaternius' rigged dogs (CC0, models/real/LICENSES/quaternius-dogs.txt): one skeleton, clips Walk, Gallop, Idle, Idle_2, Idle_2_HeadLow, Eating, Attack, Idle_HitReact_Left/Right and Jump_ToIdle.
- `DOG_HUSKY = "res://models/real/animals/husky.glb"`
- `CAT = "res://models/real/animals/cat.glb"`: Quaternius' Cat (CC0, models/real/LICENSES/quaternius-cat.txt), rebuilt by tools/blender/make_cat.py: clips Idle, Walk, Trot, Run, Stalk, Crouch, Pounce, Sit, Loaf, Groom, Sleep, Hiss, Startle and Stretch, and the coat fields cat_coat.gdshader reads.

### Functions

- `static func first_existing(paths: Array) -> String`: First path in the list that load_scene() can load, or "".
- `static func load_scene(path: String) -> PackedScene`: The PackedScene at path, or null. Returns non-null only when ResourceLoader.exists(path) is true, load(path) is non-null and the result is a PackedScene. Cached per path.

## `scripts/fp/body_contacts.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Contacts of a box body on the ground plane (a car) with the walker's world: CollisionWorld's boxes and cylinders that reach above the body's step and start below its roof, and ground it cannot drive onto (water and the bridge parapets, where walk_height is NAN, or a rise above WS.STEP_HEIGHT). Shared by the player's car (drive) and the cars it shoves (traffic). Points are Vector2(x, z); contacts are OBB2D's [normal, depth, point], the normal pushing the body out.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `OBB = preload("res://scripts/fp/obb2d.gd")`
- `PROBES = [0.004, 0.012, 0.025, 0.045, 0.07]`: A blocked outline sample looks for drivable ground this far out along an axis (u), then bisects between the last blocked and the first free probe.
- `BISECT = 4`
- `AXES = [Vector2(1, 0), Vector2(-1, 0), Vector2(0, 1), Vector2(0, -1)]`

### Functions

- `static func gather(col: CollisionWorld, c: Vector2, reach: float, feet: float, height: float) -> Dictionary`: The obstacles a body with its feet at `feet`, `height` tall, can meet within `reach` of c: {"boxes": Array[AABB], "cyls": PackedFloat32Array of (x, z, r), "ground": true when the tiles around c hold ground it cannot drive onto (outline samples are tested only then)}.
- `static func contacts(col: CollisionWorld, obs: Dictionary, c: Vector2, yaw: float, h: Vector2, feet: float) -> Array`: Contacts of the box (centre c, yaw, half extents h = (half width, half length)) with the gathered obstacles, and with undrivable ground when the gather found some, in no order.
- `static func ground(col: CollisionWorld, c: Vector2, u: Vector2, v: Vector2, h: Vector2, feet: float) -> Array`: Contacts with ground the box cannot drive onto, from samples round its outline: a blocked sample is pushed back along the axis (every such edge in the city runs along x or z), toward the box's middle, where drivable ground is nearest.
- `static func outline(c: Vector2, u: Vector2, v: Vector2, h: Vector2) -> PackedVector2Array`: Twelve points round the box: its corners, the middles of its ends and three more along each side.
- `static func drivable(col: CollisionWorld, p: Vector2, feet: float) -> bool`: True when a body with its feet at `feet` can drive onto the ground at p.

## `scripts/fp/city_directory.gd`

class_name `CityDirectory` · extends `RefCounted`

Human place names for the city: streets for road runs, addresses for lots, business and landmark names, district names. Deterministic from sim.city_seed; never uses sim.rng.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `STREET_NAMES = [ "Maple", "Oak", "Cedar", "Birch", "Willow", "Elm", "Pine", "Aspen", "Chestnut", "Laur...`
- `AVENUE_NAMES = [ "Addison", "Barrett", "Calloway", "Delgado", "Easton", "Fairview", "Grafton", "Halsey...`
- `SURNAMES = [ "Alvarez", "Brooks", "Chen", "Dubois", "Edwards", "Fischer", "Garcia", "Haddad", "Ito...`
- `ADJECTIVES = ["Golden", "Blue", "Corner", "Little", "Lucky", "Green", "Daily", "Bright", "Copper", "...`
- `KINDS = { D.ZONE_C: { 1: ["Cafe", "Bakery", "Bookshop", "Florist", "Diner", "Barbershop", "Deli...`
- `LANDMARK_SUFFIX = { D.POLICE: "Police Station", D.HOSPITAL: "General Hospital", D.SCHOOL: "Elementary Sch...`
- `RUN_CAP = 32`: Contiguous road tiles counted in each direction when measuring a run.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim) -> void`: Binds the sim and builds the seed permutations.
- `func rebuild() -> void`: Recomputes the seed-dependent permutations (call after load / New City; cheap).
- `func street_name(i: int) -> String`: Name of the street a road tile belongs to ("Maple Street", "Delgado Avenue"); for a junction the name of its longer run. "" for non-road tiles.
- `func intersection_name(i: int) -> String`: "Maple Street & Delgado Avenue" for junction tiles (3+ arms), else street_name(i).
- `func frontage(i: int) -> int`: The road tile lot i fronts (4-neighbour ROAD with the longest run; ties S, E, N, W), or -1.
- `func frontage_yaw(i: int) -> float`: Yaw in degrees that turns a model's +Z face toward frontage(i) (S=0, E=90, N=180, W=-90); NAN if none.
- `func address(i: int) -> String`: "214 Maple Street" for a lot with frontage; "" otherwise.
- `func business_name(i: int) -> String`: Business name for a ZONE_C / ZONE_I tile at level > 0 ("Alvarez's Bakery"), else "".
- `func business_kind(i: int) -> String`: "bakery", "warehouse", ... for C/I lots at level > 0, else "".
- `func landmark_name(i: int) -> String`: Landmark name for a service tile ("GridFall City Hall", "Maple Street Fire Station"), else "".
- `func place_name(i: int) -> String`: Best name for a tile: landmark, business, apartment name (R2/R3 "Maple Court"), else "".
- `func place_label(i: int) -> String`: Best label for a tile: place_name, else address, else street_name, else district_name.
- `func district_name(i: int) -> String`: District name: D.MAYORS[d]["district"] for claimed land, "the river" on water, else "the frontier".
- `func mayor_display(d: int) -> String`: Mayor display name for district d (D.MAYORS[d]["display"]), "" for d < 0.
- `func street_at(p: Vector3) -> String`: Street label for a world point: road -> intersection_name; lot -> its frontage street; else the nearest road within 2 tiles; else district_name.
- `func planned_name(i: int, target_kind: int, target_level: int) -> String`: The name tile i will carry once a construction site finishes as (target_kind, target_level): the same rules as landmark_name / business_name / place_name, computed for the target instead of the current kind. "" when the target has no name (roads, R1 houses, demolition).

## `scripts/fp/forest_trees.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

The woods' synthetic trees. city_view.gd plants them by exactly this hash (its tree chunks: N trees on every in-bounds forest tile), so the animals that climb them — squirrels first, cats bolting from a charging dog — find a trunk that is really drawn. The forest tiles carry no colliders, so this hash is the only way to know where their trunks stand.

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `N = 4`: The trees a forest tile keeps, how far (u) off the tile's middle they fall, the size step between them, and a street tree's trunk radius (u) they scale from (they draw at 1.0 to 1.6 times a street tree).
- `SPREAD = 0.85`
- `STEP = 0.1`
- `TRUNK_R = 0.25 * WS.M`

### Functions

- `static func tree(gx: int, gz: int, t: int) -> Array`: The t-th tree the view plants on the forest tile (gx, gz): its world xz and trunk radius [x, z, r]. The tile's own hash, so the answer never moves.
- `static func nearest(p: Vector3, i0: int, r: float, kinds: PackedInt32Array) -> Array`: The nearest wood tree to p within r (u), as [x, z, r], or [] for none: the forest tiles of the 3x3 neighbourhood of tile i0 are enough for any r up to a tile and a half. kinds is the sim's kind array (PackedInt32Array).

## `scripts/fp/fp_context.gd`

class_name `FpContext` · extends `RefCounted`

Service locator for first-person slices. FpMode fills it once in setup(); fields never change identity until FpMode.teardown() (CityView keeps its identity across view.setup()).

### Constants

- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`

### Properties

- `main: Node3D`: main.gd; call main.save_game(), main.focus(), main.notify(), main.exit_fp()
- `residents: Residents`: may be inactive (GRIDFALL_RESIDENTS=0): check residents.is_active()
- `env: Environment`: the shared Environment (Main.camera.environment), mutated by SkyDirector
- `world_root: Node3D`: FpMode/World: put in-world FP nodes here, never under CityView
- `features: Dictionary`: feature_id -> FpFeature
- `settings: Dictionary`: see FpMode.DEFAULT_SETTINGS; change only via mode.apply_settings()
- `ws: GDScript`: convenience; prefer your own `const WS := preload(...)` for typing

### Functions

- `func feature(id: String) -> FpFeature`: The registered feature with this id, or null.
- `func push_modal(owner: StringName) -> void`: A UI that needs the mouse and keyboard (chat input, pause menu, map, dialogue) pushes itself; while any owner is pushed, the player ignores movement and look, and the mouse is visible. Emits bus.modal_changed(true) on 0 -> 1.
- `func pop_modal(owner: StringName) -> void`: Removes owner; emits bus.modal_changed(false) on 1 -> 0.
- `func is_modal() -> bool`: True while any modal owner is pushed.
- `func has_modal(owner: StringName) -> bool`: True while owner is pushed.
- `func modal_count() -> int`: Number of pushed modal owners.
- `func player_position() -> Vector3`: Feet position of the player (world units). Without a player (some unit tests): mode.spawn_point().pos when mode is set up, else Vector3.ZERO.
- `func player_tile() -> int`: Tile index under the player (D.idx), or -1 outside the world.

## `scripts/fp/fp_feature.gd`

class_name `FpFeature` · extends `Node3D`

A first-person feature module owned by one slice. FpMode instantiates it from the registry, adds it under FpMode/Features (Node3D at identity, so children are in world space) and drives the lifecycle: setup -> on_world_rebuilt (after every view.setup) -> to_dict/from_dict -> teardown.

### Functions

- `func feature_id() -> String`: Stable id; also the key in ctx.features and in save["fp"]. Override.
- `func setup(p_ctx: FpContext) -> void`: Store ctx, connect signals, build nodes that do not depend on the city geometry.
- `func on_world_rebuilt() -> void`: The city view was rebuilt (boot, load, New City). Re-attach anything tied to tiles.
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: Feature state for save["fp"][feature_id()]. Return {} for nothing.
- `func from_dict(_d: Dictionary) -> void`: Restore state; d is {} for a fresh city or an old save.
- `func teardown() -> void`: Disconnect from long-lived objects (sim, view, residents, brain, bus); FpMode frees the node after.
- `func pick(_origin: Vector3, _dir: Vector3, _max_dist: float) -> Dictionary`: Interaction pick along a ray (A's interact queries every feature). Return a target dict (§9) or {} when this feature owns nothing on the ray within max_dist.
- `func self_test() -> Dictionary`: Called by the FP smoke after the world is up. {"ok": bool, "detail": String}.
- `func photo_shots() -> Array`: Extra named eye-level shots for the FP photo tour: [{"name": String, "pos": Vector3 (feet), "yaw": float deg, "pitch": float deg, "hour": float, "prepare": String (optional), "restore": String (optional)}]. "prepare" / "restore" name methods on this feature that the tour calls (no arguments) before the shot is placed and after it is saved, for example forcing rain and clearing it again.
- `func link_signal(sig: Signal, c: Callable) -> void`: Connects c to sig (once) and remembers the pair for unlink_signals().
- `func unlink_signals() -> void`: Disconnects every pair link_signal() connected whose source is still alive. Call from teardown.

## `scripts/fp/fp_mode.gd`

class_name `FpMode` · extends `Node3D`

First-person composition root: builds the context, bus, player, collision, HUD and every registered feature, owns time controls, pause, the mouse and the FP save section.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `REGISTRY = preload("res://scripts/fp/fp_features.gd")`
- `SETTINGS_PATH = "user://gridfall_fp_settings.json"`
- `DEFAULT_SETTINGS = { "mouse_sensitivity": 0.0022, "invert_y": false, "fov": 72.0, "head_bob": true, "quali...`: camera_mode is "third" (over-the-shoulder, the default for play, D13) or "first"; "fov" is the first-person FOV and "tps_fov" the third-person one; shoulder is 1 (right) or -1 (left); hero is "m" or "f". fp_kit.make_ctx overrides camera_mode to "first" unless a test asks otherwise.
- `RESERVED_KEYS = ["version", "player", "time_scale", "day_phase"]`: Save keys FpMode owns; a feature id must not use them.
- `SAVE_VERSION = 1`

### Properties

- `settings_log: Array[Dictionary]`: Every patch passed to apply_settings, in order (tests read it; also filled when not set up).
- `capture_mouse: bool`: False keeps the pointer free (scripted tours and benchmarks; GRIDFALL_FP_PHOTO_DIR or GRIDFALL_MOUSE=free), so a windowed test run never grabs the desktop pointer.
- `auto_low_quality: bool`: The quality preset came from GpuMemory's low mode, not from the player's saved settings.

### Functions

- `func setup(main: Node3D) -> void`: Builds everything. main is the Main node (main.gd); reads its sim, residents, minds, brain, client, view, sky, audio, camera and sun_light fields.
- `func teardown() -> void`: Tears down the features (reverse order) and the HUD, releases the mouse, unpauses.
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: Save section, see S0 §6.4. day_phase is how far the current 300 s growth tick has run (0..1): the sim saves only whole ticks, which would rewind the FP clock by up to 6 game hours.
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`: Restores the save section. {} means a fresh city: player at spawn_point(), features reset, and the tick phase at 0 (also for saves without day_phase).
- `func set_time_scale(s: int) -> void`: Sets the sim speed to s, snapped to WS.TIME_SCALES; emits bus.time_scale_changed. Paused: stored, applied on resume.
- `func step_time_scale(dir: int) -> void`: +1 / -1 through WS.TIME_SCALES (bound to time_faster / time_slower).
- `func skip_to_morning() -> void`: Runs the rest of today's ticks now, so the next day starts at 06:00 (bound to time_skip). Coroutine: toasts "Skipping to morning...", awaits 2 frames, then calls sim.skip_to_next_day().
- `func set_paused(p: bool) -> void`: Pauses the whole SceneTree (get_tree().paused). The FpHud and FpMode keep running. Emits bus.pause_changed.
- `func apply_settings(patch: Dictionary, persist: bool = true) -> void`: Appends patch to settings_log, merges it into ctx.settings, saves SETTINGS_PATH (skipped when setup() never ran, as in fp_kit's stub mode, or when persist is false, as for the photo tour's and fp_bench's camera override), emits bus.settings_changed(settings) and, if "quality" changed, bus.quality_changed(preset).
- `func spawn_point() -> Dictionary`: Feet position and yaw for a fresh player: the sidewalk in front of City Hall (S0 §7.3). {"pos": Vector3, "yaw": float (deg)}.
- `func unstick_player() -> bool`: Moves the player out of any building or site box they stand in (one can appear on the lot they stand on) to the nearest free point, else to the spawn point. True if the player was moved.

## `scripts/fp/game_bus.gd`

class_name `GameBus` · extends `Node`

Signals that cross first-person slices. Emitters and listeners are listed in docs/fp/S0-foundation.md §9.

### Signals

- `ping(world_pos: Vector3, reason: String)`: A world point that deserves attention (y = 0). reason: "event:<type>", "resident:<id>", "tile", "district:<mi>", "ai:<mi or support role>" (an AI decision landed there) or "player" (a waypoint set on the map).
- `toast(text: String, kind: String)`: A player-facing notice. kind: "info", "alert", "success" or "system".
- `interact_target_changed(target: Dictionary)`: The interaction target under the crosshair changed; {} when nothing is targeted.
- `interact_requested(target: Dictionary)`: The player pressed interact on target.
- `talk_requested(resident_id: String)`: The player asked to talk to a named resident.
- `conversation_changed(resident_id: String, active: bool)`: A face-to-face conversation started or ended.
- `chat_posted(msg: Dictionary)`: A message was posted to the global chat (chat message dict, §9).
- `poster_ready(poster: Dictionary)`: A poster texture is ready: {"key", "kind", "texture", "meta"}.
- `player_tile_changed(x: int, y: int)`: The player entered tile (x, y).
- `time_scale_changed(scale: int)`: The first-person time scale changed (1, 2, 4 or 8).
- `settings_changed(settings: Dictionary)`: The settings changed; settings is the full dict.
- `pause_changed(paused: bool)`: The game was paused or resumed.
- `quality_changed(preset: String)`: The quality preset changed: "low", "medium" or "high".
- `modal_changed(active: bool)`: Some modal UI opened (true) or the last one closed (false).
- `world_ready`: The world was rebuilt and every feature ran on_world_rebuilt().
- `card_action(action: String, tile: int)`: A button on a place card: action "ask_here" (C answers through brain.inspect_tile). Emitted by B.
- `drive_changed(active: bool)`: The hero got into a car (true) or out of it (false). Emitted by the drive feature.
- `car_impact(at: Vector3, speed: float, what: String)`: The player's car hit something hard: the contact point, the closing speed (u/s) and what was hit, "wall" (anything fixed) or "car". Emitted by the drive feature.
- `car_door(at: Vector3, open: bool)`: The driver's door of the player's car opened (true) or slammed shut (false), at its handle. Emitted by the drive feature.
- `prop_knocked(at: Vector3, kind: String, speed: float)`: A street prop was knocked over, or a fallen one kicked hard, at a point (its StreetDressing kind: "bin", "cone" ...) and flies off at speed (u/s): by the player's car, the hero, people walking, traffic or another prop. Emitted by the props feature.
- `person_hit(at: Vector3, cause: String, info: Dictionary)`: Someone on foot was hit at a point (their feet): cause "shove" or "punch" (the hero's fists and kicks), "car" (the car the player drives) or "carjack" (dragged out of the car the player takes); info is traffic_feature.gd hit_walker()'s {"walker", "resident_id", "name", "down", "street", "strength", "witnesses", "crew"}, a throw that meets a wall or a solid prop mid-flight adding "impact" {"at", "in"} (throw_impact — marked on this one emission, never a second person_hit). Emitted by traffic.
- `hero_action(action: String, at: Vector3)`: The hero swung, gestured or got over something: action "jab", "cross", "hook", "shove", "kick", "swing" (a weapon in hand), "counter" (a hook countering a punch), "throw" or "slam" (someone held), "grapple" (taking hold of someone), an emote ("wave", "yes", "no", "shout", "dance") or a parkour move ("vault", "hop", "climb", "roll" off a hard landing, "grab" taking hold of a wall, or free running's "run_up" up a ledge, "catch" of a ledge in the air and "leap" across a gap), or "hijack" (leaping from the car the hero drove onto one to take), as it starts, at their feet. Emitted by the actions, brawl, parkour and drive features.
- `horn_sounded(at: Vector2, radius: float, long: bool)`: The hero's car horn sounded at at (street plane, xz): radius is how far it carries in world units, long true when the hero leans on it (a tap first, the held press turning long). Emitted by the drive feature (the horn_street flag); the street's answer to it -- people startled, birds up -- lives with the agents that draw them.
- `weapon_hit(at: Vector3, kind: String, what: String, broke: bool)`: A weapon in the hero's hand landed a blow at a point on what ("person" or "prop"): kind "bat", "pipe" or "bottle", broke true when it broke (a bottle does on its first). Emitted by the melee feature.
- `animal_hit(at: Vector3, kind: String, strength: float)`: A blow of the hero's (a kick or a weapon) landed on an animal at at: kind "dog", "cat" or "pigeon", strength 0..1. Emitted by the animals feature.
- `talk_replied(resident_id: String, speaker: String, reply: String)`: Someone answered the hero: a resident face to face (their id and name), or whoever answered "Ask someone here" (resident_id "" and their role, "Shopkeeper"). reply is filtered for display. Emitted by chat.
- `story_filed(story: Dictionary)`: The player filed a story for the Gazette: reporter_feature.gd file_story()'s {"agent", "headline", "place", "quote", "by", "tile", "district", "day", "scoop", "local", "sharp", "points", "text"}. Emitted by the reporter feature; chat runs "text" as a Gazette line.
- `hero_hit(at: Vector3, cause: String, strength: float, push: Vector3)`: Something struck the hero on foot: at is where the blow came from (a fist, a car's front, a dog's jaws), cause "punch" (someone fighting back), "car" (a car that could not stop for them) or "bite" (a dog defending its owner), strength 0..1 and push the xz velocity (u/s) it throws the hero along. Emitted by traffic and the animals feature; the health feature takes the damage.
- `hero_threatened(at: Vector3, secs: float, wid: int)`: Someone fighting the hero (wid, the walkers_near id) started a punch from their fist at that lands in secs, unless the guard goes up in time to counter it (the actions feature's parry). Emitted by traffic.
- `hero_slammed(at: Vector3, what: String, over: bool)`: The hero slammed the person they held into something (the brawl feature's slam): at is the contact at chest height, what "wall" (a wall, a post or a parked car) or the street prop's kind, over true when the prop went over with them. Emitted by the brawl feature.
- `hero_hurt(amount: float, cause: String, health: float, down: bool)`: The hero lost amount of health to cause: "punch", "car" or "bite" (hero_hit), "crash" (in the car they drive) or "fall" (a hard landing); health is what is left (0..100, 0 knocked out) and down is true when it put them on the ground. Emitted by the health feature.
- `animal_called(at: Vector3, call: String, size: float)`: An animal called out at a point (its head): a dog's "bark", "growl" or "whine", a pigeon's "coo", a lone pigeon's "flap" or a flock's "takeoff", a cat's "meow", "purr", "hiss" or "chatter" (at a bird it stalks); size is its height at the shoulder (m), so a small dog yaps higher. Emitted by the animals feature.

## `scripts/fp/obb2d.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

Oriented boxes and circles on the ground plane, as Vector2(x, z): overlap tests, contacts and inertia for the player's car body and the street props it knocks over. A box is its centre, its unit axes u and v (perpendicular) and its half extents along them, Vector2(along u, along v). A contact is [normal, depth, point]: the unit normal that pushes the first shape out of the second, how far it has to go, and a point of contact inside the overlap.

### Constants

- `EPS = 1e-6`: A corner this close outside the other box's faces still counts as inside it (u).

### Functions

- `static func side_axis(yaw: float) -> Vector2`: A box's local +X axis at yaw (heading +Z at yaw 0, as for every vehicle).
- `static func heading(yaw: float) -> Vector2`: A box's local +Z axis at yaw: its heading.
- `static func box_inertia(h: Vector2, m: float) -> float`: Moment of inertia about its centre of a solid box with half extents h and mass m.
- `static func near_rect(p: Vector2, r: float, lo: Vector2, hi: Vector2) -> bool`: True when the circle round p of radius r reaches into the rectangle lo..hi.
- `static func box_box(ca: Vector2, ua: Vector2, va: Vector2, ha: Vector2, cb: Vector2, ub: Vector2, vb: Vector2, hb: Vector2) -> Array`: Contact of box A (centre ca, axes ua va, half extents ha) with box B, or [] when they do not overlap. The normal is the separating axis of least overlap; the point is the mean of the corners of either box inside the other (the midpoint of the centres when none are).
- `static func box_aabb(ca: Vector2, ua: Vector2, va: Vector2, ha: Vector2, b: AABB) -> Array`: box_box() with the xz footprint of an axis-aligned world box.
- `static func box_circle(ca: Vector2, ua: Vector2, va: Vector2, ha: Vector2, c: Vector2, r: float) -> Array`: Contact of box A with the circle round c of radius r, or [] when they do not overlap. The point is the box's point nearest the circle's centre.
- `static func corners_inside(c: Vector2, u: Vector2, v: Vector2, h: Vector2, oc: Vector2, ou: Vector2, ov: Vector2, oh: Vector2) -> PackedVector2Array`: The corners of box O (centre oc, axes ou ov, half extents oh) that lie inside box C.

## `scripts/fp/road_topology.gd`

class_name `RoadTopology` · extends `RefCounted`

Static road-tile helpers shared by collision, traffic, the directory, the minimap and the streetscape. They mirror CityView._road_mask / _road_piece exactly: mask bits N=1, E=2, S=4, W=8 with north at -Z; straight runs N-S, corner joins S+W, tee joins E+S+W, end opens S.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `WS = preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`
- `N = 1`
- `E = 2`
- `S = 4`
- `W = 8`
- `NS = 5`
- `EW = 10`

### Functions

- `static func mask(sim: CitySim, x: int, y: int) -> int`: Neighbour mask of road tile (x, y): ROAD neighbours only, exactly like CityView._road_mask.
- `static func piece(m: int) -> Array`: [piece: String, yaw_deg: float] for a mask; piece in straight|corner|tee|cross|end. Mirrors _road_piece with real roads present.
- `static func arms(m: int) -> Array[Vector2i]`: Unit directions (dx, dy) of the open arms, in N, E, S, W order. dy is world +Z.
- `static func is_carriageway(m: int, lp: Vector2) -> bool`: True when local point lp = (wx - x, wz - y) of a road tile with mask m is on the carriageway.
- `static func grade(sim: CitySim, i: int) -> int`: Grade of road tile i (D.ROAD_GRADES, kept in its level); paved for bridges and non-roads.
- `static func paved(sim: CitySim, i: int) -> bool`: True when road tile i is a paved street (curbs, sidewalks, street furniture).
- `static func surface_height(sim: CitySim, i: int, lp: Vector2) -> float`: Walkable surface height at lp on road tile i: ASPHALT_TOP on the carriageway, SIDEWALK_TOP on the sidewalk, NAN outside the bridge parapet (bridge = ROAD on WATER terrain, straight only). Unpaved grades have no curb: the whole tile is ASPHALT_TOP.
- `static func sidewalk_point(sim: CitySim, i: int, side: int) -> Vector3`: World point at the centre of the sidewalk on `side` (+1 right, -1 left of the run) of a straight road tile. The run points north (-Z) for N-S tiles and east (+X) for E-W tiles, so +1 is east of a N-S run and south of an E-W run. y is SIDEWALK_TOP (ASPHALT_TOP on the verge of an unpaved road).
- `static func run_dir(m: int) -> Vector3`: Unit run direction of a road tile with mask m: east (+X) when it has only E/W arms, else north (-Z).
- `static func run_right(m: int) -> Vector3`: Unit vector to the right of run_dir(m).
- `static func is_bridge(sim: CitySim, i: int) -> bool`: True if road tile i is a bridge (ROAD on WATER terrain).

## `scripts/fp/scene_loads.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

PackedScenes loaded on background threads (ResourceLoader's threaded loads), for the features that stream bodies in (the crews' workers, the dogs): request() starts a load, scene() hands the scene out once it is in, and finish() waits for the loads still in flight. Without real threads (the no-threads web build) request() loads on the caller's thread instead.

### Constants

- `WebSupport = preload("res://scripts/ops/web_support.gd")`

### Functions

- `func request(path: String) -> void`: Starts loading the scene at path on a background thread (once), or at once when there are none.
- `func pending(path: String) -> bool`: True while the scene at path is still on its way.
- `func scene(path: String, wait: bool) -> PackedScene`: The scene at path once it is in; null while it loads (unless wait, which blocks until it is in) or when it failed. Asks for it first when nobody did.
- `func finish() -> void`: Waits for the loads still in flight (quitting with one running aborts it noisily).

## `scripts/fp/world_scale.gd`

extends `RefCounted`

First-person world scale. One unit is one tile is 20 m; physical quantities are written as metres * M. Preload as WS: `const WS := preload("res://scripts/fp/world_scale.gd")`. Values are frozen (docs/fp/S0-foundation.md §4.3): a slice adds constants only inside its own section at the end of this file.

### Constants

- `M = 0.05`: units per metre (core.py:19 M = 1/20)
- `TILE_M = 20.0`: metres per tile
- `EYE = 1.65 * M`: 1.65 m standing eye height (ARCH §2)
- `CROUCH_EYE = 1.0 * M`: 1.0 m crouched eye height (ARCH §2)
- `PLAYER_RADIUS = 0.3 * M`: 0.3 m capsule radius (ARCH §2)
- `PLAYER_HEIGHT = 1.8 * M`: 1.8 m standing height
- `CROUCH_HEIGHT = 1.2 * M`: 1.2 m crouched height
- `WALK = 1.45 * M`: 1.45 m/s (ARCH §2)
- `RUN = 4.5 * M`: 4.5 m/s (ARCH §2)
- `CROUCH_WALK = 0.8 * M`: 0.8 m/s
- `ACCEL = 10.0 * M`: 10 m/s², ground acceleration
- `GRAVITY = 9.81 * M`: 9.81 m/s² (crit §d)
- `JUMP_SPEED = 3.4 * M`: 3.4 m/s, apex about 0.59 m
- `STEP_HEIGHT = 0.25 * M`: 25 cm max auto step; clears the 12 cm curb
- `MOUSE_SENSITIVITY = 0.0022`: radians per pixel (default setting)
- `PITCH_LIMIT_DEG = 85.0`
